# Reuse is a claim about coverage the tests were never asked to support
# again. The rules deciding it are the one part of this tool that can quietly
# report a suite as stronger than it is, so --verify checks them: it runs every
# mutant even when the state has an answer, and fails when the answer was wrong.
#
# Run it in CI on a schedule. It costs a full run, and it is the only thing
# that can catch a reuse rule that has drifted.

muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1
cmp stdout want-first.txt

# An honest state file verifies clean, and says how much it checked.
muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1 --verify
cmp stdout want-verified.txt

# Now make the file lie: the mutant was killed, the record says missed.
cp lying-state.txt testdata/template-mutations.json
! muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1 --verify
cmp stdout want-disagreement.txt
stderr 'recorded MISS, found KILL'

# The file was rewritten with what the run found, so it no longer lies.
muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1 --verify
cmp stdout want-verified.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "greeting"}}Hello, {{.Name}}!{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Name string
}

func Greet(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreet(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Greet(&buf, Page{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want-first.txt --

1 mutant, 1 killed, 0 missed, 0 skipped
-- want-verified.txt --

baseline ok
